mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP indicates strong economic growth, which positively impacts corporate earnings and drives S&P 500 forward returns higher over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, which is positive for consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the unemployment rate falls below 4% but the S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When both payroll employment and the unemployment rate improve simultaneously, it indicates a robust labor market, leading to increased economic activity and higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If both payroll employment and the unemployment rate improve but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, which can lead to decreased borrowing and spending, resulting in lower S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate rises above 4.5% but the S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 40% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production indicates higher economic output, which is positive for corporate revenues and leads to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in retail sales suggests strong consumer demand, which is positive for corporate revenues and leads to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If retail sales growth exceeds 5% in 3 months but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 30% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low and GDP growth is strong, it indicates an accommodative monetary policy supporting economic growth, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the federal funds rate is low and GDP growth is strong but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 35% of the next 20 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts indicates expanded construction activity and economic growth, leading to higher S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If housing starts increase but S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 40% of the next 60 trading days, this hypothesis is rejected.
